title: Harbor: conversational Azure serverless KT (IoT Hub, Functions, Cosmos DB)
proves: Casual phrasing and serverless architecture place correctly.
transcript:
Hey, thanks for jumping on. So Harbor is our fleet telemetry thing, it takes readings from about thirty thousand delivery vans.

Everything is serverless on Azure. The vans send readings to IoT Hub, an Azure Function picks them up and writes them into Cosmos DB, and a second function rolls them up into Azure Data Explorer for the dashboards the fleet managers use.

The code lives in GitHub and we deploy with GitHub Actions straight to the function apps. There is a staging slot, and we swap it into production.

For alerts we rely on Application Insights, and the one that matters is the function failure rate going over five percent, which posts to the on-call Teams channel.

Biggest gotcha: Cosmos DB throttles when the vans reconnect after a network outage, and the readings pile up. Bump the RU limit for an hour and it catches up.

Please never delete the IoT Hub consumer groups, the analytics team reads from them.

We keep two environments, staging and prod, and staging uses a simulator instead of real vans.

Cosmos has continuous backup turned on, but we have never actually tried a restore.

The fleet platform squad owns all of this, and escalation goes to Mia Chen.

We spend a lot on Cosmos, so the RU limits are scaled down overnight.
